1.Content: 瑟恩，你还撑得住吗？

2.Content: 我没事。

1.Content: 小鹿，你还撑得住吗？

2.Content: 我没事。

0.Content: Whaaaah! Help, help!

1.Content: Huh? Are you here for the legendary Dwarven treasures too?

2.Content: There are no treasures whatsoever! There's nothing here but traps!

3.Content: They must've set traps to protect the treasures. I'll go in and check it out.

4.Content: Hey, wait!

0.Content: What's that sound? Oh? Have I stepped on something?

1.Content: You just triggered a trap... Look there! Now the road ahead is completely blocked!

0.Content: Whoa... Over there!
I see, if we trigger a trap that blocks our way, all we need to do is find the right Deactivation Tower to undo the blockage.
My feet feel so warm, have you noticed too?

1.Content: Ah! This is a hot spring!

0.Content: We meet again. Is there anything I can help you with? Or could it be that you already found another diary page?
You have my thanks, now let's take a look at your findings. Hmm... This entry is quite interesting. Although it is filled with complaints, it must be written by a humorous person... um, a Hypogean.

1.Content: Allow me to thank you once more, my friend. I feel this diary will prove quite useful in my search for my lost memories.

0.Content: More diary pages? I must say, your diligence is truly remarkable... However, these pages don't seem to match the ones you previously gathered for me.

1.Content: In fact, these diary entries seem to be from an age long past. They mention a pari of ancient weapons... I've heard tales of that time, an era where humankind waged war against the gods of this world.

0.Content: I can't be certain whether or not they will help... But you are free to bring me more of them, if you have the chance.

1.Content: For the longest time, my missing memories have weighed heavily on my heart... But my mentor would reprimand me whenever I asked her about my past, saying that a Celestial's duty is to uphold justice and order in the world.

2.Content: But with your help, I pray that my questions will finally be answered.

0.Content: I... I am forever in your debt, friend.

1.Content: For the longest time, my missing memories have weighed heavily on my heart... But my mentor would reprimand me whenever I asked her about my past, saying that a Celestial's duty is to uphold justice and order in the world.

2.Content: But with your help, I pray that my questions will finally be answered.

0.Content: Welcome back, friend. It seems your adventure today was quite fruitful... I can only imagine the incredible things you witness throughout your travels.
The gods always remind me that if my piety is lacking, the turmoil and temptations of the outside world will lead me astray from the Divine Light.

I appreciate your concern, but perhaps we should just focus on the diary pages you've brought me today... Hmm? So the weapons were a pair of children all along! I wonder what became of them? It seems we won't know until we gather more pages.
Hello, again. Thank you for helping me gather so many pages in such a short amount of time.
Nothing important, I'm afraid... But I knew the search for my lost memories wouldn't be easy. I'm prepared to go on without them, if need be.

We are... Not permitted to feel any unnecessary emotions, especially for ourselves. Mortals are free to do so, but as the protectors of truth and justice, we mustn't let anything cloud our sense of judgement.
How kind of you to say so... But I am merely performing my divine duties.

Have you brought me even more pages today? Let me see... Aha! It says here that the two children were eventually found and raised in a loving home. You know, I often wonder what it must be like to grow up as a mortal child...
Tell me, do these treats taste... Pleasant?
Would that be acceptable? I mean... N-Never mind... Thank you for your gracious offer, but with the specter of war looming before us, I don't have time to indulge in such things.
Again, your generosity is most appreciated... But the gods say that we must restrain our selfish desires, lest they lead us astray.
Forgive me, my friend. I was lost in thought just now, and failed to notice your arrival.
I was merely wondering what I could do to ensure our victory in the current battle...
Rest assured, I am perfectly within my own limits. Now then, shall we take a look at the pages you've brought me today? Hmm... Yes, these entries are crucial to my search.

1.Content: Thank you again, my friend. I will keep your suggestion in mind... But for now, I must focus on the growing threat of the Hypogeans. I wish you safe travels, friend.

0.Content: Thank you for bringing me even more diary pages, friend. Perhaps we'll learn more about those two children? Let me see...

1.Content: I'm shocked that a Hypogean could show so much compassion towards two children... From what I've been told, they are cunning and wicked beings that are incapable of such behavior, but this "Eugene"... He seems different.

0.Content: Your words are quite profound... I must confess, I sense something different about that female Hypog... that girl. She doesn't seem evil in any way at all. In fact... There's something strangely familiar about her.
I feel as though my convictions are beginning to falter... Forgive me, my friend, but I need to be alone right now.
You've returned! Tell me, did you find any more clues about the fate of those two children?
Yes, but why is that? At times, I cannot help but feel as though I share some sort of connection with them...

1.Content: Let's just read through today's entries...Oh good, it seems they were ultimately rescued by the gods... Urgh! M-My head... What is this pain?!

0.Content: It was vague, but I recalled something just now. A person was shouting my name, telling me to seek a certain girl... But who could she be? Forgive me, I just need a moment to compose myself...
Thanks to the diary pages you just brought me, I finally understand the origin of this entire story. The war between humans and gods... I had no idea it was like this.

1.Content: My memories are as unclear as ever. I knew retrieving them would be no easy feat, but...

Don't let it trouble you, friend; you've done more for me than you know. While my memories continue to elude me, you've taught me so much about friendship. To know that someone cares about me like this... Is truly comforting.

0.Content: Thank you, my friend. May the Divine Light always protect you.
Huh? Back already? Oh my, you're way quicker than any of these bumbling Hypogeans! I knew I was right about you!
Hey! This "kid" happens to be your commander, so show some respect! Besides, you wouldn't have done so well without my brilliant guidance, so let's see what you found!

1.Content: Hah! This "Eugene" guy sounds like a ton of fun, unlike those Celestial pigeons over there. Say, I kind of like that! I think I'll call them "pigeons" from now on!

2.Content: Now hurry up and find me some more diary pages! I'm bored out of my mind over here—er, I mean, I need more information for the upcoming battle!

0.Content: Ugh, finally! Do you know how long I've been waiting?
W-Wait! Don't get the wrong idea! Why would a mighty Hypogean commander wait around for a bumbling idiot like you? Makes no sense at all!

Y-You've got it all wrong! Anyways, what's with these diary pages you found? They don't have anything to do with the last ones! In fact, this one looks like it was written ages ago... And not by that Eugene guy.

1.Content: Looks like this diary was written by someone two thousand years ago... So the humans picked a fight with the gods back then, huh? Pretty brave of them... I bet the gods were way tougher than those pigeons over there!

2.Content: I'm not sure if these diary pages will help me get my memories back, but I might just remember something if we manage to find them all.

0.Content: Another new diary entry? You sure are a hard worker... Now hand it over!

1.Content: This one's from Eugene, and it looks like they ran into some trouble... Dang, who would've guessed that the ancient weapons were a pair of kids? That's awesome!

2.Content: Even after reading all of these pages, I still don't remember anything... Ugh, what an annoying feeling!

3.Content: Hey... Do you think there's something wrong with me? It feels like I've forgotten something really important, but I can't remember squat!

0.Content: Yeah, maybe you're right... But you never heard me say that, got it? I just wanna know how these stories end. It's not because I'm desperate or anything.
Sniffle, sniffle...
Hahahaha! Gotcha, dummy! Come on, I thought you were smarter than that!
Stop being so sentimental. I don't need any friends. You're being such a nag today…

1.Content: You alright? I hear there are lots of dangerous monsters out there, just waiting to tear adventurers to pieces... Not that I care about you or anything, though! Now let's see those pages!

0.Content: Back already? Not bad, not bad... You're pretty good at this, you know?

These two kids were pretty lucky... I can tell Eugene and his pigeon buddy really cared about them. They're almost like... Almost like... Ugh, I can't really describe it, but it makes me feel a little jealous.
A "family"? What the heck is that?
So even if you're not the biggest, baddest Hypogean around... A family will still love you? That sounds kinda nice...
It's been a while, huh? Run into anything exciting out in the world?
Really? I feel like I've seen a spider like that before... Wait, why the heck would you bring me something like that?!
Ah, but since you want to be friends so badly, I guess I could put up with a crappy gift like that. Just get me something better next time, okay?

1.Content: Oh, and before I forget, let me take a look the pages you found this time.

2.Content: So that stinkin' alchemist was the one who turned those kids into living weapons, huh... What a scumbag. If I was alive two thousand years ago, I would've personally taught that jerk a lesson.

0.Content: Hey, you're back! Gosh, it feels like ages since the last time I saw you. Did you bring me more pages to read? I'm dying to know what happened to Eugene and his pigeon friend after they got separated!

1.Content: What?! It says here that the kid got seriously hurt... Did they manage to survive? They were so little... I just hope Gavus found a way to save them.

2.Content: Hey, remember that Celestial kid I fought last time? For some reason, something about him feels really familiar...

3.Content: It won't be long until our next battle, and I'm sure it's gonna be a big one. I won't have time to protect you when it happens, so just remember to take cover.

0.Content: Ahem... J-Just try not to make more trouble for me. I've got your back now, so if anyone wants to mess with you, they'll have to go through me first!
Did you find any more pages? I have to know what happened to those kids!

Yeah... They remind me of myself somehow, but they were way better off than me. Even though they had to deal with so many problems, at least they had nice guys like Eugene and Gavus to look out for them.

1.Content: Let's see what it says here... No way! Gavus took the kids to the Celestials in order to save them! But why? Those rotten pigeons couldn't be trusted at all!

2.Content: Urgh! Damn... Why does my head hurt, all of a sudden?! Wait, something's happening...

0.Content: It was vague, but I recalled something just now. A person was shouting my name, telling me to protect a certain boy... But who was he? Ugh, my head's killing me... Just give me a second, okay?

I just finished reading through the stuff you brought me. I can't believe that lousy alchemist was the one who started all of this! So many people got hurt because of that lunatic, including innocent children!

1.Content: I don't know what became of Eugene and the others, or if those Celestials were able to save the kids... I just hope they were able to go home and live happily ever after. At least then I'd feel better about my own crappy situation...

0.Content: It's kinda hard for me to say, but... I've learned a lot from you in the time that we've known each other. I'm sure you've noticed by now, but I'm no stranger to loneliness...

1.Content: But after you showed up, I learned just how fun it is to have a friend! Sure, it sucks that I didn't get my memories back... But at least I have an idea of what it's like to have family now.

2.Content: I guess what I'm really trying to say is... Thank you. You're a good friend, and I'll always remember you.

0.Content: Dear adventurer, I gather you are here for the Noctis Animarum Festival? What do you reckon kids like to play with these days?
Jack o'Lanterns? I happen to know a great Jack o'Lantern workshop. They can definitely make one that Daimon will like.

Welcome to Fantasy Hut! On the first floor, you can use Candy Keys to draw Jack o'Lantern accessories, then you can proceed to the second floor to customize your Jack o'Lantern or assemble them any way you like.

1.Content: But I'm planning to move... since monsters have appeared around here recently.

0.Content: Leave the monsters to me. Keep your shop running. Many children are looking forward to your Jack o'Lanterns!
This space-time rift... It is how the monsters traveled to our realm.

1.Content: If the crisis is not resolved soon, the Noctis Animarum Festival may not go on as usual. And Daimon would be so disappointed.

0.Content: When my mom return, we'll join the Noctis Animarum Festival together! Adventurer, I also wish you fun and joy on Noctis Animarum!
The fabric of time and space around the Realm of Denial grows unstable, and the night when the spirits roam among mortals draws near. Cracks form between worlds, granting me entry into reality.

1.Content: [Shemira becomes aware of a series of extinguished bonfires in the wilderness and advances forward.]

2.Content: There are coordinates carved onto this stone... Did someone leave this behind?

0.Content: These powerful Soul Flames are particularly useful in the Realm of Denial. You should keep an eye out for them.
What kind of place is this?! I've been walking in circles!

1.Content: This is the Realm of Denial. This plane of existence is distilled from the obsessions of the lost souls of the deceased who cannot let go.

2.Content: How did I end up here?!

3.Content: Look, we're not far from reality here. I'll show you.

4.Content: Hmm... This is something I picked up here. It should be useful for you.

0.Content: Thank you.
No need to be so polite. C'mon, we can exit through this crack.

1.Content: ... When did she leave her present behind?

0.Content: [Shemira arrives in a wind-swept desert.]

1.Content: [There is a dying traveler. His eyes are full of despair as he clutches an empty water skin.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this situation is the distillation of what the thirsty traveler still clings to from his previous life.]

0.Content: Thank you for the food and water... I feel much better now.

1.Content: Just rest. You don't need to speak.

2.Content: No, I need to find my companions... They're waiting for me...

3.Content: Ah, so this is what you're clinging to... I'm afraid there's nothing I can do for you.

4.Content: You're too kind.

0.Content: Help me! Help me! I'll give ten thousand gold to anyone who helps me!

1.Content: Poor child. Come and shelter with me.

2.Content: [Shemira deals with the monsters effortlessly. Then, she squats down to comfort the quaking child behind her.]

3.Content: Don't be scared. You're fine now.

4.Content: T-Thank you... But... I don't have ten thousand gold...

0.Content: It doesn't matter. I didn't save you for the gold... I have a child, too...

1.Content: I'm sorry I lied to you. Please take my last gold coin.

2.Content: Alright, let's go. I'll take you home.

0.Content: You lying little brat! I should throw you back to the monsters!

1.Content: Please don't! I still have one gold coin! Please forgive me!

2.Content: I guess I'll just have to accept it. C'mon, I'll take you home.

0.Content: The fabric of space and time is even more chaotic around here. Looks like we're even deeper into the Realm of Denial now.
[Shemira arrives in a burning room.]

1.Content: [There is a young man hacking at the collapsed beams with an axe. It looks like he is trying to escape. At his side, there is a crying child.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this situation is the essence of what the father can't let go of from his previous life.]

0.Content: Thank you, my lady. Thank you for saving my child. I can finally put this axe down.

1.Content: You will complete your journey with your child.

0.Content: Hello, have you seen a warrior with dazzling blonde hair? That's my companion. We got separated around here.

1.Content: I'm sorry, I haven't. Time and space are warped here. It's not easy to find anyone.

2.Content: Yeah... Well, if you see him, tell him that I'm waiting for him at the old road sign.

0.Content: If I see him, I'll let him know.

1.Content: Even though I know you're not likely to run into him either, thank you very much all the same.

2.Content: Don't lose faith. I must continue on my way. Farewell.

0.Content: Honestly, it's not a good idea. Any road sign may have already changed locations.

1.Content: You're right. All I can do is hope that we'll meet in the Realm of Denial again. Farewell.

0.Content: We're in a very strange place, aren't we?

1.Content: Yeah, you shouldn't have come here.

2.Content: No. The stars will guide me, and they'll help you move forward... Farewell, for now.

0.Content: Till next time...

1.Content: Will the stars tell her that she's lost something?

0.Content: [Shemira arrives by an empty lakeside.]

1.Content: [There are two Graveborns in the middle of a fight. They are two brothers who fell out long ago, and now they're fighting over a past they can't let go of.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this is the place where their clinging to the past converges.]

0.Content: [Shemira stays clear of the brothers and quietly leaves. Shemira finds some useful items by the road.]
[Shemira holds the brothers back, blocking them from fighting, and sends them both back to their individual realities. Then, Shemira picks up the items that they left behind.]
That's a dense thicket of thorns, but it should be easy to deal with...
I hope that father has already found peace.
[Shemira arrives at the precipice of a cliff.]

1.Content: [There is an adventurer lying on the ground, reaching towards the cliff. She's trying to pick the blooming flowers from beneath the cliff, but there is always just a little distance between her fingers and the flowers.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this situation is the result of what the adventurer can't let go of from her previous life.]

0.Content: Let it go. These flowers aren't the healing Goldflares.

1.Content: Really? Please help me up then.

2.Content: [Shemira helps the adventurer back up to her feet.]

3.Content: *Gasp*... Thank you, I almost fell. But I'm still going to find those Goldflares.

4.Content: Sorry for the trouble caused. Goodbye.

0.Content: I'll hold your hand, and you can reach further down.

1.Content: Alright, thanks!

2.Content: [Shemira holds the adventurer and helps her pick the flowers from the cliff.]

3.Content: Hey... now that I have them in my hand, I realize that these aren't the Goldflares I was looking for. Never mind. I will keep searching.

4.Content: Sorry for the trouble caused. Goodbye.

0.Content: [Shemira arrives in a pitch-black cave. There are beautiful paintings and carvings all around, but they are half buried under rocks and sand.]

1.Content: [There is a treasure hunter trying to move a stone. The treasure is right under his nose, but he can't see it. His movements are making the already collapsed cave even more unstable.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this situation is the distillation of what the treasure hunter can't let go of from his previous life.]

0.Content: Hey! Look around you!

1.Content: Gold! Gold!

2.Content: He's totally obsessed with gold. He can't hear anything else...

0.Content: Look here. I have a gold coin.

1.Content: Gold!

2.Content: This place is collapsing! Quick, c'mon!

3.Content: [The Treasure Hunter quickly escapes upon realizing that the tomb is about to collapse.]

4.Content: So he could run fast after all... If only he hadn't been blinded by everything around him, he wouldn't have been trapped...

0.Content: Get yourself together! That's a mirage created by a demon! It's not your family!

1.Content: But... No, I have to keep searching.

2.Content: You...

3.Content: [Shemira faces the two fighters and smiles softly while walking forward.]

4.Content: Well done! You've found your lost companion.

5.Content: I'm happy to see you. However, we're planning to go our separate ways.

6.Content: Yeah, she wants to follow this small path to go and check out that mirage. I want to keep on fighting the nearby demons.

0.Content: It sounds like a good idea.

1.Content: With recent flux in time and space, we might run into each other again.

2.Content: Once this night has passed, everything here will return to normal, and the souls of the dead will return to where they came from. Maybe we will meet outside of the Realm of Denial.

0.Content: There's a lot of dangers around here. It's best to stick together.

1.Content: Thanks for your advice, but that mirage looks just like my family. I might be able to find some clues about them there...

2.Content: Well... All I can do is wish you well. I hope you find what you're looking for.

0.Content: [The route is blocked by an iron box. There seems to be a creature banging loudly inside and struggling fiercely.]

1.Content: Why is there a box here? What's that noise...?

0.Content: A little kitty? What sort of a monster would lock a little cat in a box like this?

1.Content: [The terrified little cat jumps out, revealing a mask at the bottom of the box.]

2.Content: This mask has a lot of demonic energy around it.

0.Content: [Shemira arrives near a surging sea. What is unusual is that there is an alley above the sea. A bunch of rats come running from the garbage in the alley.]

1.Content: [A battered and bruised sailor is floating in the sea. She reaches out weakly as if she wants to grab someone's hand.]

2.Content: [Shemira understands that this situation is the distillation of what the sailor can't let go of from her previous life.]

0.Content: Wake her up

1.Content: [The sailor floating in the water opens her eyes. The alley above the sea suddenly turns to seafoam and vanishes in the sunshine.]

2.Content: You... I kinda... forgot someone important...

3.Content: Do you wish you could remember?

4.Content: I don't know...

5.Content: Well, you can leave this place.

6.Content: [The drowned sailor's illusion dissipates. She is about to leave the Realm of Denial and go to where her soul is supposed to go.]

0.Content: We meet again... Look where the stars led us.

1.Content: Can you still see the stars from here?

2.Content: We're quite alike, you and I. We don't just see the world through our eyes.

3.Content: I can also see that you're not a greedy person...

0.Content: Thank you for your kindness. I bring you the stars' guidance.

1.Content: The stars fluctuate, turning into thousands of faces. The cycle of reincarnation begins again, and long-cherished wishes are fulfilled.

2.Content: Okay... I don't quite get it, but it sounds like good news.

0.Content: We meet again. I've dealt with the nearby monsters, but I'm worried about what lies ahead even deeper inside this place.

1.Content: The deeper we go, the more distorted time and space become. You're right to be worried.

2.Content: The danger just keeps getting worse around here. Why do you want to keep going deeper?

0.Content: I want to attend the Noctis Animarum Festival with my child. It's his dream...

1.Content: But if these cracks in space and time are left unchecked, monsters will keep on getting through to reality, and the festival won't be able to take place anyway.

2.Content: You really are a brave mother. I wish you success on your journey.

0.Content: There are some personal matters I need to sort out. Take care of yourself. Till next time.

1.Content: Till next time.

0.Content: This is the Realm of Denial's deepest level, something might catalyze all unrelenting attachments. Lost souls collide incessantly, making space and time even more chaotic than before.

1.Content: That strange mask... What the Stargazer said...

2.Content: You don't need to hide anymore. You're the one causing the chaos around here!

0.Content: Here's the workshop I prepared for you. Please craft some beautiful pumpkin decorations—Bantus is expecting nothing less than perfection.
Your Majesty, I've found a Spirit Summoner who can help us uncover memories from the past.

1.Content: To explore the memories of the dead, you must enter the mysterious spiritual realm through my crystal ball. There will be many dangers—are you ready to face them?

2.Content: I do not fear ghosts of the past.

0.Content: Back then, we were just kids who loved Noctis Animarum and decorating pumpkins.

1.Content: Theowyn always loved carrying her little flower.

2.Content: As for Edwin, he was full of hope back then.

0.Content: When Theowyn was young, she was often sickly but we found ways to cheer her up.

1.Content: Poor thing... She must have felt awful at the time, but still, she flashed the sweetest smile.

0.Content: Edwin, I should have realized it sooner—being only a prince must have gnawed at you, little brother.
As the crown heir's brother, your loyalty had to be earned through triumphs on the battlefield.
While ascending the throne, I was too busy to carve pumpkins with you.

1.Content: From that moment on, I was no longer just an older brother but the king of a nation.

0.Content: Perhaps my biggest regret was sacrificing Theowyn. If I had made a different choice, maybe everything would be different.
By that time, Edwin's ambition was fully exposed.
That was probably the last Noctis Animarum we observed. Not long after that...
Your Majesty, did you find the answers you sought in the crystal ball?

1.Content: I recalled only a few trivial things, but I do feel much lighter.

2.Content: Reward the Spirit Summoner. As for the others, let them revel in the Noctis Animarum Festival.

0.Content: Is this the "spiritual realm" that summoner spoke of? She'd better not be fooling me.

1.Content: Hmm... something about this place feels familiar. But... what is it? Seems like the chaotic thoughts and memories in my mind have taken shape here.

0.Content: A graveyard... For the children of Bantus, this place is all too familiar.

1.Content: Fathers and brothers left for war and never returned... loved ones fell ill... But we learned to endure.

0.Content: I remember this place—in the autumns of my youth, Edwin and I rode across the former royal hunting ground, practicing for the hunt until we were old enough to enter the battlefield.
This hunting ground used to be a paradise for birds and beasts, but in the empire's later years, it became a battlefield.

1.Content: Countless soldiers' remains, unable to be returned home, were hastily buried here.

0.Content: This place is a strategic pass deep within the empire. Edwin and I once defended this ground together, holding off the enemy.

1.Content: We fought side by side, unstoppable, and earned the people's favor after that victory.

0.Content: After the battle for the pass ended, I had no choice but to marry Theowyn to the Crown Prince of Thalonia to ease tensions.

1.Content: The wedding feast was held in this very castle.

0.Content: After Theowyn's marriage, I became consumed with state affairs. Although Edwin helped me, our different approaches to governing only grew larger.
When Edwin began to let the army dabble in necromancy, I had no choice but to confine him within the palace.

1.Content: Not long after, Theowyn returned home for the Noctis Animarum Festival, and I lifted Edwin's house arrest at her request.

0.Content: Good sir, tis the season for ripe pumpkins! Look how big and shiny mine are. Please buy some if they catch your fancy!
[Thoran casually tosses a few gold coins at his feet and picks up a pumpkin.]

1.Content: Hmm, I've long forgotten the taste of pumpkin, but this shape and size is just right for carving with little ones.

0.Content: This is my spiritual realm, and all within it belongs to me.

1.Content: [Thoran snatches a pumpkin, and in an instant, the farmer and his stall vanish.]

0.Content: [Thoran arrives at a broken bridge, now overgrown with wild grass, speckled with unique little purple flowers.]
Bantus, once blooming with flowers, feels like a distant memory.
Oh! Sorry, traveler, I almost bumped into you. How far are we from Bantus?

1.Content: The fog was too thick earlier, and I lost my way. I'm delivering urgent medicine to a patient.

0.Content: Oh? Then I can still make it in time. The commander entrusted his daughter to me, and I can't let illness take her!

1.Content: [The knight gallops off, disappearing into the fog.]

2.Content: Even if you save her this time, how long can you truly protect her?

0.Content: No, that can't be true! Have I come too late?

1.Content: I have failed you, Commander...

2.Content: [The knight, defeated and disheartened, turned to dust and was carried away by the wind.]

0.Content: [Thoran arrives at a wide square. A loud bugle sounds from somewhere in the distance.]

1.Content: [A formation of soldiers advances toward Thoran through the fog.]

2.Content: This is Bantus' former army. With such troops, our iron hooves once trampled the surrounding nations.

0.Content: No one can stop the advance of Bantus' army; even to the last man, our forces will complete their mission.
[Thoran draws his sword to face the army. As the formation moves closer, he realizes that the soldiers are mere phantoms. They pass through Thoran's body before vanishing.]

1.Content: I remember now; this is the parade ground of Bantus' former army, where countless soldiers set out to defeat our enemies.

0.Content: Old friend, today we settle this. The winner will become the Guardian of the Forest and marry the old guardian's daughter.

1.Content: Of course! I won't hold back. When the king next calls for war, I'll lead our village to victory.

0.Content: [The archer and hunter duel honorably. Evenly matched, at the signal, their weapons strike each other at once, and they both fall dead on the spot.]

1.Content: Serving Bantus was the highest honor—a glory worthy of sacrificing one's life to achieve.

0.Content: [A wounded brown bear blocks Thoran's path, baring its teeth and growling fiercely, as if ready to pounce.]
[Just as Thoran raises his great sword to strike the bear, a spear flies in from the side, hitting the bear and sending it fleeing.]

1.Content: Great! I've hunted a bear! If I bring this trophy back, perhaps Father will pass the title to me instead of my cowardly brother!

0.Content: [Thoran stays still. Shortly after, the sound of hoofbeats grows closer. The bear flees as a group of royal guards appear, chasing it.]

1.Content: Everyone, stay sharp! This bear is meant to be hunted by the Earl's son. No one is allowed to interfere!

0.Content: [As Thoran continues forward, a young boy suddenly bursts from the side of the road, crashing into him.]

1.Content: Ouch! Oh, sorry traveler, I didn't mean to bump into you. If anyone asks if you saw me, please say no!

2.Content: [With that, the boy dashes off, vanishing quickly. Moments later, a young girl runs up.]

3.Content: Hello, sir. Have you seen a boy with a red nose pass by?

0.Content: So he did run this way! I heard he's being sent to boarding school. I had a plan to hide him, but now that he's run off, I might never find him again.
Really? I just wanted to say goodbye. I heard that when children get sent to military boarding school, sometimes they never come back...
[A wounded carrier pigeon lies before Thoran. On closer inspection, it's covered in injuries, and its wing has been pierced by an arrow.]
[The message reveals a loyal servant warning his young master that his family hid his father's illness to exclude him from the inheritance.]
[Thoran arrives at the edge of a cliff, where he discovers assassins are setting up an ambush, with logs and explosives aimed at the valley below.]

1.Content: Who are you? If you know what's best, leave now!

0.Content: [Thoran draws his sword, swiftly dispatching the assassins. Looking down into the valley, he realizes the group below are merely refugees.]

1.Content: I remember Edwin slipped into the refugee group, infiltrating the enemy's camp and capturing their leader.

2.Content: Could our plan have been leaked?

0.Content: [Thoran stands by, allowing the assassins to launch their surprise attack.]

1.Content: Damn it, the target fled. How are we going to report this to our employer?

2.Content: [Thoran looks down into the valley and realizes the group below are merely refugees. Although heavily injured, a few have survived.]

3.Content: Employer? Edwin was among those refugees, but he left the valley to plan a surprise attack with me. Who would hire assassins to ambush refugees?

0.Content: [Thoran arrives at the ruins of a church, which was once grand but now lies in disarray.]
This is the church where Theowyn was born, once welcoming believers from all around. Before it was destroyed in the war, we visited this valley every year.

1.Content: But the year I was preparing for my ascension at the royal court, only Edwin and Theowyn came.

0.Content: [Near a dry well, a multi-headed skeleton mutters at a charred tapestry.]

1.Content: I see a beauty drawn here, truly a stunning maiden!

2.Content: I see a terrifying shadow—it's the Grim Reaper!

3.Content: And you, traveler, what do you see?

0.Content: The tapestry shows a bride on her wedding day.

1.Content: But the more affection she receives, the more destruction she brings.

0.Content: The tapestry shows a deathly beast, eager to devour everything in its path.

1.Content: Who would set this creature among helpless lambs?

0.Content: [Thoran enters the castle, which is deserted and dilapidated. Its former splendor is nowhere to be found.]

1.Content: [As Thoran prepares to leave through the garden, he finds the exit blocked by three thick vines.]

0.Content: [Thoran draws his great sword and strikes at the vines with all his might, but they're entwined like a web. After many hacks, he manages to clear them, only to realize that the three vines all share a single root.]
[Thoran approaches the cellar and finds the shared root of the three vines in the dim light. When he touches the root, the vines crumble to dust and blow away.]
[Next to an abandoned farm, two farmers are pulling a sickly cow, arguing heatedly.]

1.Content: This cow is old and sick! If we keep it alive, it'll infect the other cattle. It has to be slaughtered!

2.Content: No! The cow can still be saved... It just needs rest, food, and the right treatment.

3.Content: But all that costs money and time. It'll ruin the farm! Traveler, what do you think?

0.Content: Useless things just burden you. It should be put down, and what's left can still be of use.

1.Content: That's right! Even if it worked hard for us for over ten years, in the end, it's just a beast—a tool.

0.Content: You can't just kill it. With some time and care, it might recover.

1.Content: No matter how much it costs or delays our harvest, I'll save it. After all, without it, we wouldn't be here today!

0.Content: [Under the dim night sky, Thoran comes to a wide lake. Across the water, he notices a flickering light.]
[Thoran follows the light away from the lake. As he gets closer, he realizes it's a fisherman using a shining coin as bait.]

1.Content: The biggest fish in this lake only go for shiny things.

2.Content: I'm using my last coin as bait, hoping to catch that big one. If I don't, I'll be left with nothing...

0.Content: [By a long staircase, a child is absorbed in a book. As Thoran approaches, the child looks up to ask him something.]

1.Content: Hello, traveler. I'm reading about the history of this continent. Have you heard of a country called Bantus?

2.Content: I know it well; I come from Bantus.

3.Content: What kind of country was it?

0.Content: It sounds like a place everyone dreams of, where the people are happy.

1.Content: To maintain the empire's strength, every citizen must fulfill their duties; happiness is not a necessity for Bantus.

0.Content: After all this time, it's probably gone forever, turned into dust.

1.Content: My empire has been reborn in another form. Today's Bantus is a presence that terrifies the entire continent.

0.Content: [Thoran arrives at his destination, a house glowing with warm candlelight, filled with the joyful laughter of children.]
[As Thoran opens the door, the candlelight and laughter fade. A roughly carved Halloween pumpkin with tiny purple roses sits on the dusty dining table.]
Do you think working overtime is an honor?
Of course! Overtime is a way to show our dedication to the company. I feel proud to do what I can.

1.Content: Hmm, that's what I thought! Only hard work pays off. We must give our all for the company.

0.Content: I think overtime just drains people. It doesn't get more work done—it's a waste of time.

1.Content: W-What?! How dare you say that! That's an outright attack on company culture!

0.Content: If the company ordered you to work 48 hours straight, what would you do?
I'd throw myself into completing the task. I'm willing to sacrifice everything for the company.

1.Content: That's the spirit! Giving up personal time is the only way to create true value for the company. That's what a loyal employee does.

0.Content: That's insane. No normal person can work for 48 hours straight. An employee's health comes first.

1.Content: No! You can't think that way! That's treason against the company!

0.Content: Do you think giving up vacation days should be every employee's responsibility?
Of course! The company gives us purpose. Sacrificing our days off helps us do our jobs better. After all, true loyalty is giving our all.

1.Content: Hearing you say that makes me feel less alone. Everyone should be as committed to the company as you are.

0.Content: Vacation time is an important part of being an employee. Skipping it just makes people burnt out and less productive in the long run.

1.Content: What's this?! You dare disagree with the company's values?! You don't belong here!

0.Content: Company culture emphasizes "sacrificing yourself for the greater good." How do you interpret that?
It means giving up your personal life to create maximum value for the company. It's for the greater good.

1.Content: You really get the company spirit! What a model employee! It's a joy working with you!

0.Content: That sounds unreasonable. Employees' personal lives and health matter too. Work isn't everything, you know?

1.Content: You're a troublemaker! You need reeducation! Take them to the Reflection Room and let's fix that attitude!

0.Content: Mezoth, step forward!

1.Content: What did you just say?! You lowly grunt... I'm the CEO's relative, you know!

2.Content: Still smug after that last beating? Your days of slacking off are over. It's time to take orders and do some real work!

3.Content: The employee cafeteria is low on supplies. You're on grocery duty.

4.Content: Hmph! We'll see about that.

5.Content: Hey, traveling merchant! I'm Mezoth, Head of Security!

6.Content: Oh wow, the big boss himself running errands?

0.Content: You've got a deal!

1.Content: Didn't really think I'd say that, huh?

2.Content: Huh?!

3.Content: I got word from your company—they're cracking down on corruption and you've been demoted.

4.Content: Still trying to take kickbacks? Looks like I'll have to report you.

0.Content: Alright, alright! Thanks for your business. Since you're a regular, I'll even throw in a discount.

1.Content: And be sure to say hi to your new boss for me!

2.Content: Ugh, just thinking about that wretched plant makes my blood boil!

0.Content: Argh! What more do you want from me?!

1.Content: With the company restructuring, you're now on security duty.

2.Content: But given how much you've been lying around and stuffing your face, first we think you need some serious physical training.

3.Content: Find yourself a trainer... it's for your own good.

0.Content: A Hypogean's aura? I didn't expect you'd come knocking! Let's see if you can handle my sword!

1.Content: Huff... huff... am I being too hard on myself?

2.Content: [Some time later]

3.Content: Well, look at that! You've actually got a pep in your step!

4.Content: You have no idea what I just went through!

0.Content: Yaaawn... What? Training? How about we start with a little nap...

1.Content: Now this is my kind of trainer!

2.Content: [Some time later]

3.Content: I don't see a shred of effort. Nope, you're not meeting our standards.

0.Content: We need some fresh ideas for the Dream Realm. Ezizh, as the former Head of Design, you must've collected a bunch, right?

1.Content: Heh... The old designs? A pile of garbage. Not a single one worth using.

2.Content: That's because your briefs were a mess. Well, now's your chance—pitch us a new concept.

0.Content: Hahaha... To break the mold, you need to think from a different angle.

1.Content: Tell me more.

2.Content: The new plan? Change the Dream Realm's main character. Instead of the usual heroes, why not put minor villains or background characters in the spotlight?

3.Content: Like you—a lowly grunt rising up against the odds. What do you think of that theme?

4.Content: Me? Hmm... that actually sounds kind of interesting. Alright, let's roll with it!

0.Content: How about making the bosses tougher? Give heroes a real challenge!

1.Content: Eh, that doesn't sound like a game-changer. That idea's a dud.

0.Content: With all the nonsense requests out of the way, our efficiency has skyrocketed. We're finally open to external projects!

1.Content: Buuut... the other designers are all on vacation, so this job falls to you.

2.Content: Pffft. I don't do low-quality projects.

3.Content: You don't get a say in this. It's time you learned how hard design work really is!

4.Content: I want a fantasy theme park—a magical place straight out of a fairytale!

6.Content: Oh, and it should also be educational.

8.Content: And it needs to have exciting rides that are completely safe.

10.Content: It'd be great if adults could enjoy it too!

11.Content: This is way too much for one person!

12.Content: There's no time to waste—start drafting the proposal for the village elder!

0.Content: Done! Old man, here's the proposal I pulled an all-nighter to get it just right!

1.Content: Hmm... Something feels off. Can you try again?

2.Content: What do you mean feels off?!

0.Content: Fine, old man! Here, take ten proposals! Look through them yourself!

1.Content: Can you walk me through them in detail?

2.Content: I've never had a tougher client!

3.Content: (Ezizh explains the first proposal.)

4.Content: Hmm... It's not very exciting. Can I hear the others?

5.Content: (Ezizh goes through the remaining nine, sweating and flailing wildly.)

6.Content: You know what? The first one was actually pretty good. Let's go with that.

0.Content: We need a new song for the latest Dreamscape. You're the perfect person for the job!

1.Content: Isn't that the design team's job? Why are you coming to me?!

2.Content: We believe in breaking down the department's barriers and letting everyone play to their strengths!

3.Content: Here's my concept. I need you to compose a soundtrack for it.

0.Content: Yes, yes! This is exactly what I was going for!

1.Content: What are you talking about? I haven't even finished tuning my strings...

2.Content: No, this is perfect! It's absurd yet sorrowful, with chaos brewing underneath!

3.Content: I feel inspired!

4.Content: Why do I feel like his head's not quite right...

0.Content: Wait... This sounds kinda familiar.

1.Content: That's because it's the same song! Can you take this seriously?!

0.Content: I've been here for years, and every annual company event is a snoozefest. This year, we've got to fix it.

1.Content: You're dreaming... No matter how you dress it up, it's just corporate brainwashing.

2.Content: No way! You were all about control and exploitation. We're not against company structure, we just want a fair and open system!

3.Content: Hah! You remind me of my younger self when I first joined.

4.Content: Ugh, that's unsettling... So, do you have any fresh ideas for the event?

0.Content: Hmm... I heard you were a bassist in a band before joining. What song would you play for us?

1.Content: Of course my greatest hit, "Overtime Is Amazing!"

2.Content: Yeah, no thanks. That would be even worse.

0.Content: So you're saying we should make the event rewarding for employees?

1.Content: Exactly! That way, they'll stay engaged and even look forward to it.

2.Content: Huh... Maybe there's more to you than just brainwashing your way to the top.

0.Content: The moment I was launched from that cannon, I didn't feel fear... I felt... relief.

1.Content: If we tweak it a bit, this could make for a fantastic attraction!

2.Content: Framton, as the cannon specialist, can you help me modify it?

3.Content: Well, well... You've got guts for a little potted plant. If you had followed me from the start, you'd already be my right-hand man.

4.Content: Yeah, no thanks.

5.Content: Hmph! Fine. I'll help you out.

0.Content: The modifications are complete! Mwahaha! Alright, little plant, hop in!

1.Content: I've been blasted enough times today. Why don't you give it a go, ex-boss!

2.Content: Wait! Let me just... fine-tune it!

0.Content: To keep it safe, I reduced the gunpowder and added padding to the front.

1.Content: Now it's safe while still delivering that soaring-through-the-sky thrill!

2.Content: Perfect! This is definitely gonna be a hit!

0.Content: Marketing has been liberated, but the team leader is still scarred from years of pressure.

1.Content: Framton, as the former head of Marketing, you should apologize and help him move on.

2.Content: Survival of the fittest. He was just a weak employee!

3.Content: We're all about collaboration and freedom now. Your outdated way of thinking needs to go—apologize!

4.Content: Team leader!

0.Content: Aaaaaahhh! Nooo! Please, no more!

1.Content: I don't wanna fire another coworker into a cannon!

2.Content: Framton! You really have no remorse?!

3.Content: Sorry, force of habit. It just slipped out.

4.Content: Try again. And mean it this time.

0.Content: W-Wait... What? The former department head just apologized to me...?

1.Content: I've waited years for this moment! Suddenly, I feel lighter... The cannon blasts are gone, the sky is so blue, and the birds sing so sweetly!

2.Content: Speaking of which, team leader, we've revamped the cannon and will be opening it as an employee entertainment attraction. Can you continue managing it?

3.Content: (He foams at the mouth and loses consciousness.)

4.Content: Hmm... Looks like I should've waited a bit longer...

0.Content: Now that we've taken down the Head of Efficiency, these workshops are no longer needed.

1.Content: So, you want to humiliate me now that I'm defeated?

2.Content: Of course not. I'd like you to oversee its transformation into a building that meets our current needs.

3.Content: Such ruthless tactics! No wonder you managed to topple five departments in a row.

4.Content: I have no idea what you're talking about...

0.Content: I saw the complaints on Workplace Talk. Since everyone's so obsessed with toilets...

1.Content: I'll turn the Streamline Workshops into luxury restrooms that can accommodate a hundred people at once.

2.Content: That's actually a great idea! More restrooms, better work-life balance, and who knows? Productivity might even improve!

0.Content: Since you all had issues with my previous "Two-Step Policy"...

1.Content: Let's turn the Streamline Workshop into an assembly line. This way, every task can be done in just one step!

2.Content: That's even worse! Turning people into mindless drones isn't what we want!

0.Content: Even though the Efficiency Department is free now, our past mistakes have tanked efficiency. Unfinished reports are piling up with no one to handle them.

1.Content: Can you help take care of this task?

2.Content: Piece of cake!

0.Content: Zolrath, how's it going?

1.Content: Why rush? I've slowed down the flow of time. Now, we've got all the time in the world!

2.Content: That's just an excuse to slack off!

0.Content: You're doing nothing!

1.Content: Hmph, you just don't get efficiency. I've created a sentient clone inside my hourglass and sped up its time.

2.Content: I simply give it the tasks, and it produces the results we need in no time.

3.Content: Cutting-edge magic can change the way we work and live after all...

0.Content: Hmm... The next final boss, Kane, was supposed to debut next season, but he's on strike.

1.Content: Leofric, can you negotiate with him?

2.Content: Happy to help—that's what HR is for, after all.

3.Content: You're surprisingly cooperative.

4.Content: A wise person adapts to their situation. Let's go talk to him.

6.Content: I won't work unless I get a raise! Getting beaten up by heroes non-stop during work hours is the kind of job that deserves better pay.

0.Content: How about we track their beatings during shifts and calculate a bonus based on that at year's end?

1.Content: Sounds like another empty promise, just like the ones you made before!

2.Content: Heh, as long as it's written into the contract, it's binding. Besides, I'm no longer the Head of HR—the authority is yours now.

3.Content: You've got a point. Kane, does that work for you?

4.Content: Hmm... It sounds reasonable enough.

5.Content: Great! Then let's sign the new contract!

0.Content: Now that you're the new boss, how about a raise, effective immediately?

1.Content: The company's funds are tight after all the recent upheaval and corruption, so we can't offer a raise right now.

2.Content: And stop calling me that... I'm not your new boss!

3.Content: Haha! You've definitely got leadership potential. I'm sure you'll get used to it soon enough.

4.Content: Fine... Let's come up with another solution.

0.Content: The company is growing rapidly, and we've just welcomed our first wave of new hires.

1.Content: We need someone to handle their basic training. Can you take care of it?

2.Content: I heard this new batch of young recruits is particularly difficult to manage. Let me take a crack at them.

0.Content: That covers our company overview. Any questions?

4.Content: Sleeping on the job on day one? You're just asking to be fired!

5.Content: That would breach our employment contract and violate my personal rights. If you fire me without reason, you'll be in big trouble!

0.Content: Ahh! This is so exciting! I didn't expect our company to be this fun!

1.Content: To be honest, our company used to be a heartless business, but after making some changes, we've embraced a more joyful and free way of working.

2.Content: This is exactly the kind of company I wanted to join!

0.Content: In the past, our company was always under pressure from the higher-ups and never had the chance to learn from other companies and their systems.

1.Content: So, I'd like to ask you to help me contact some other companies and organize a corporate exchange to promote mutual development.

2.Content: You're truly unaware of how lucky you are. Once you see other companies, you'll realize how fortunate we already are.

3.Content: We'll decide for ourselves if we're happy or not. Go ahead and choose a company.

0.Content: A company led by a Graveborn? I guess that makes sense, since they often appear as villains.

1.Content: But since they're a family business, who knows? Their work environment might be even more brutal than ours.

2.Content: I've made up my mind! Let's show them what it means to be free during this exchange event!

0.Content: They're certainly a legally compliant and well-established corporation, but...

1.Content: What's the problem? Isn't legality and compliance what you care about?

2.Content: Our operations are worlds apart. Their business is based on fighting villains, which means us! I'm worried it'll cause chaos at the event...

3.Content: Let's choose another company.

0.Content: Khazard, emergency!

1.Content: What are you up to now?

2.Content: One of the team leaders hurt their back while testing the human cannonball project. Come and help!

3.Content: Ow... Ow... my back!

5.Content: Who would've thought we'd be taken down by the likes of you.

0.Content: The team leader has suffered enough. Time for me to put them out of their misery.

1.Content: Stop! I just want you to help ice the injury!!!

0.Content: Oh... That's feels much better...

1.Content: Thank you, Khazard. I guess you're not so heartless after all.

2.Content: Get this fool out of my sight!

0.Content: What's your name?
You're not on the list of monsters!
Hmm, your name is indeed here. Next question!
You look awfully young to be applying to a corporation. How old are you?
This info is wrong... Do you think you're being funny?
Hmm, ambitious for a youngster!
Final question. What's your monster ID? Don't think you can bluff your way past me!
You can't even remember your own ID number, but you think you're fit to work here?
Hmph. Looks like all your information is correct. Behave yourself and get inside!
Can't even remember your own details? Go home, memorize your resume, and come back when you're ready!

1.Content: Uh... I'll go review it right now!

0.Content: First question: I see you majored in Landscaping Design. To be frank, that doesn't align with our company's core business. It's even a bit niche. Why didn't you choose a more popular major? Your grades weren't good enough?
It's true... Dreafs aren't particularly powerful, and unlike other Hypogeans, we aren't born with evil abilities. Many other disciplines are just... too difficult for us to master.

1.Content: Hmm... We prefer candidates who can hit the ground running. Your background isn't the best fit, so it might be a stretch.

0.Content: Every skill has its place! Landscaping Design is the perfect field for Dreafs. I'm confident that when it comes to this area, no Hypogean can outmatch my kind!

1.Content: Hmm... Your confidence and reasoning are impressive.

0.Content: Why didn't you start working after graduating? You took a two-month vacation—don't you think that suggests a lack of urgency?
I took a graduation trip to recharge and prepare for the workforce. That experience broadened my horizons and strengthened my resolve to contribute to the Abyssal Realm.

1.Content: Mental preparation is important. It seems like you know how to manage yourself well.

0.Content: Oh, no, it's not like that... I take this job very seriously! I just thought... a short break before starting work wouldn't hurt.

1.Content: Sounds like an excuse. You need a clearer career plan.

0.Content: To be honest, we have many outstanding candidates this round—some from powerful Hypogean families, others with powerful evil talents. Compared to them, what's your edge?
I... I work hard.

1.Content: Hard work is valuable, but that alone won't convince me.

0.Content: I don't believe in comparing myself to them. I focus on my strengths, using my expertise in Landscaping Design to bring value to the company.

1.Content: That's a well-thought answer. I appreciate your focus and independent thinking.

0.Content: Our company runs on a tight schedule, and overtime is the norm. Especially for new hires like you, expect to handle many small but important tasks. How do you feel about that?
If overtime has a purpose, I'm willing to put in the extra hours. But if it's just pointless busywork, I believe the work process should be optimized rather than wasting employees' time.

1.Content: That's a good perspective. We need employees who think critically, not just mindless cogs in the machine.

0.Content: If needed, I'll do my best to adjust.

1.Content: "Do your best to adjust"? That sounds reluctant. We need employees who actively contribute, not just comply.

0.Content: We have strict performance evaluations. Employees who don't meet the standards will be eliminated. Can you handle that kind of pressure?
I'll do my best to meet expectations, but if the pressure becomes too much, I may need time to adapt.

1.Content: Effort is important, but if you can't handle a high-pressure environment, you won't survive here.

0.Content: I believe pressure is a part of growth. I'm ready to face challenges and turn them into motivation, finding more effective ways to work under stress.

1.Content: That's what I want to hear. Overcoming adversity is what separates winners from the rest.

0.Content: (Seeing your confident responses, the interviewer nods slightly.)

1.Content: Alright, that concludes my questions. I look forward to seeing your performance.

2.Content: Thank you very much!

0.Content: (Your responses lack confidence and the interviewer shakes their head slightly.)

1.Content: I don't think your answers were convincing.

2.Content: (You feel utterly worthless. Your vision blurs with nerves. In the end, you crumble under the interviewer's gaze.)

0.Content: Let's talk about your daily habits. I'm curious, what's your sleep routine like?
I never stay up late. Once it gets dark, I bury myself in the soil and sleep instantly!

1.Content: A Hypogean should be causing chaos around the clock! Sleeping as soon as it's dark? That's very lazy! You might not be the kind of person we need.

0.Content: I can pull all-nighters. Sometimes I don't even need sleep.

1.Content: Good. Sleeping is a waste of time for Hypogeans. Employees like you can handle our workload.

0.Content: As a Dreaf, what's your ideal living environment? If you could choose a garden to live in, what would it be like?
I just want to live in the closest garden to the company!

1.Content: Perfect! We actually have a cheap garden for Dreaf employees right by the entrance. Who cares about the environment... proximity is what really matters!

0.Content: I prefer a garden with plenty of sunlight, loose soil, and strong Arcana.

1.Content: That's pretty indulgent! Only caring about your own comfort? We need employees who prioritize the company, not slackers who just want an easy life.

0.Content: Your resume doesn't mention any hobbies. That's interesting, because hobbies often reflect a Hypogean's true self. What do you enjoy doing in your free time?
I like flower arranging and running.

1.Content: You have time for leisure? Our work should fully consume you. Hobbies? What a waste of time!

0.Content: I don't have any particular hobbies.

1.Content: No hobbies? Excellent! That means your focus is entirely on work. That's exactly the kind of employee we need.

0.Content: So, let's say you walk into the company and see a weak little Dreaf trying to compete with you. What would you do?
Survival of the fittest. I'd kick it out of the garden.

1.Content: Very good! Weaklings have no place here. If you understand that, you've got the potential to fend off competition.

0.Content: I'd help it stir up some chaos.

1.Content: Are you running a charity here? This is Infernal Enterprises, where survival of the fittest is the only rule! A Hypogean who doesn't know how to compete gets wiped out.

0.Content: Last question. Let's say you see another Hypogean getting recognized by the company and crowned "Hypogean of the Year." What do you do?
Congratulate them and learn from them.

1.Content: Ha, how naive. Learn from them? That means they'll always be ahead of you! Hypogeans don't waste time being humble.

0.Content: Work harder than them and take that title for myself.

1.Content: Good! That fighting spirit is exactly the kind of culture we foster here at Infernal Enterprises. Always ready to surpass others, that's how you reach the top of the pyramid.

0.Content: Congratulations! You've passed the final interview. Your answers were very impressive. From today on, you are officially a member of Infernal Enterprises.

1.Content: Remember, our mission is to "Overthrow the Abyssal Realm, Overthrow the Future." Good luck!"

2.Content: Phew... I finally passed.

0.Content: Unfortunately, your performance didn't meet our expectations. Failing isn't the issue... the real problem is failing to learn from it.

1.Content: Take some time to reflect, and come back when you're ready to try again.

0.Content: One person or a group—both are trapped in mortal danger. You can only save one. Will you abandon the many to save the one, or try to save them all?
Saving one's better than losing everyone...

1.Content: Hmph! So you'd leave the rest to die. Cold-blooded, aren't you...? Haha!

0.Content: I'd save them all—even if the odds are against me.

1.Content: Save everyone? That's a fool's errand. Your "best effort" is just a way to drag everyone down with you. But somehow, that comforts you, huh?

0.Content: Say you swore loyalty to someone once—but they turned evil. Would you betray them?
Yes. I won't serve evil.

1.Content: Tch... So quick to toss away your oath. Loyalty's just a pretty word to you, huh?

0.Content: No. A vow is forever and I stand by my word.

1.Content: How tragic... Like a loyal hound, kneeling beside a master who's long since lost his mind—willing to die with him just the same?

0.Content: Tell me... when someone dies, what do they really leave behind?
They leave behind their name.

1.Content: A name? It'll be forgotten. Even if it's carved on a gravestone, time will wear it away like it was never there.

0.Content: They leave behind their story.

1.Content: A story? Please. Stories are spun by the living. By the time you're gone, yours will be twisted beyond recognition.
